NEW DELHI: Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday extended greetings to devotees on the occasion of Sandhya Arghya, the third day of Chhath Puja , as authorities put in place elaborate arrangements across the state to ensure safety during the festival.Millions of devotees are expected to offer 'arghya' to the setting sun at the Ganga and other rivers, ponds and water bodies across Bihar on Sunday. The four-day festival will conclude on Monday, when worshippers will offer prayers to the rising sun.In a post on X, Choudhary wished people on the occasion and prayed for happiness, peace, prosperity and well-being in their lives through the blessings of the setting sun and “Chhathi Maiya”."Heartfelt greetings and best wishes to all on the auspicious occasion of Sandhya Arghya, the third ritual of the festival of Chhath. Jai Chhathi Maiya", he wrote.With large gatherings expected at rivers and other water bodies, the Bihar Disaster Management Department has deployed disaster response personnel and local volunteers across the state to handle emergencies and facilitate rescue operations.According to an official statement, quoted by PTI news agency, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel have been deployed at 254 ghats, while National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams are stationed at 123 ghats. Local divers and 'Aapda Mitras', or disaster response volunteers, have also been deployed at 12,806 ghats.The arrangements include the deployment of divers and disaster response teams at water bodies during the third and fourth days of the festival, when devotees offer prayers to the setting and rising sun while standing in water.
Article Summary: Millions of devotees expected to offer 'arghya' to the setting sun at the Ganga and other rivers, ponds and water bodies across Bihar on Sunday. Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary extended greetings to devotees on the occasion of Sandhya Arghya.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BJP MLA Kishtwar Shagun Parihar criticised J&K authorities over the handling of the mortal remains of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) killed in Kishtwar district. She alleged that their bodies were brought to the area in a dumper truck and handled with indignity."You brought the bodies of our people here in a dumper truck... Is this the value of our jawans?" Parihar said while interacting with police personnel over the recovery and transportation of the bodies. She also questioned why senior officials had not responded sooner to the families' concerns."It has been three days... If an officer allows our mortal remains to be treated with indignity, what do you think the terrorists will do to them?" she said, expressing anguish over the treatment of the deceased personnel.The BJP MLA also spoke about the family members of the slain SPOs, saying that a daughter who had been waiting for her father's body. "I keep thinking of that daughter who has been weeping for the last three days... A daughter who lost her father—she came here today, three days later, and only after the LG himself asked her," she said."You didn’t even show up here until we approached the Lieutenant Governor—until we knocked on the doors of the authorities in Delhi," Parihar alleged, adding, "with a heavy heart i must say our officers our officers were disrespected".Speaking later, Parihar also demanded an inquiry into the transportation of the bodies in a dumper truck, saying that anyone who sacrificed their life for the country deserved respect and a dignified farewell. "There should be an inquiry and investigation into the officers and everyone involved, so that such incidents are not repeated," she said.The bodies of Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Bobby Chand, 57, were recovered from the remote forests of Kishtwar on Thursday. Both were residents of Kiyar Dachhan and were posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) in the Kiyar sector.The two SPOs had gone missing on November 10 while travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah for rotation duty. A search operation was launched after they failed to reach their destination. Their bodies were found with bullet injuries, while their service rifles were missing.
Article Summary: BJP MLA Kishtwar Shagun Parihar criticised J&K authorities over the handling of the mortal remains of two Special Police Officers. She alleged that their bodies were brought to the area in a dumper truck and handled with indignity. She also questioned why senior officials had not responded sooner to the families' concerns.

NEW DELHI: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge on Sunday said the law was on the state's side in the ongoing dispute over the proposed Mekedatu dam project on the Cauvery river . Kharge went on to add that that both Karnataka and Tamil Nadu would have to abide by the Supreme Court 's directions."The Tamil Nadu PCC president will make statements and do everything within his capacity to protect Tamil Nadu's interests. Similarly, the Karnataka PCC president, the Chief Minister and all of us are duty-bound to protect our state's interests," he said.He further added: "Irrespective of our individual views, the Supreme Court has given directions, and the law is on our side. Whatever happens, it is going to benefit both states. In fact, Mr Shivakumar had offered the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister an opportunity to have a dialogue on this... Everyone has to follow the law of the land".His remarks come amid a row over the project, with the BJP accusing the Congress of adopting different positions in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Senior BJP leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Karnataka Assembly, R Ashoka, on Sunday alleged that the Congress was using the state's water rights for political gains while its leaders in Tamil Nadu were opposing the project.Ashoka pointed to Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president B Manickam Tagore's description of the Mekedatu project as illegal and his appeal to chief minister C Joseph Vijay to take legal steps to prevent its implementation. He also cited Tamil Nadu Congress MP Jothimani's opposition to the project.Accusing the Congress of double standards, Ashoka said the party had earlier organised a Mekedatu padayatra in Karnataka under the slogan 'Our water, our right', but had remained silent over opposition from its leaders in Tamil Nadu."Padayatra in Karnataka, legal battle in Tamil Nadu! Slogans in support of Kannadigas in Karnataka, a fight against the rights of Kannadigas in Tamil Nadu! What should one call this double standard of the Congress?" he said in a post on X.On Saturday, Shivakumar had reiterated the Karnataka government's commitment to pursuing the Mekedatu balancing reservoir project, maintaining that the state had the right to build the dam while protecting Tamil Nadu's share of Cauvery water.He said Karnataka would seek the necessary clearances and proceed in accordance with the Supreme Court's directions.What is the Mekedatu project?The Mekedatu project is a proposed multi-purpose balancing reservoir across the Cauvery river near Kanakapura in Karnataka's Bengaluru South district. It is intended to meet Bengaluru's drinking water requirements and generate hydroelectric power.Tamil Nadu has consistently opposed the project, expressing concerns that its implementation could affect the state's share of Cauvery water.
Article Summary: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge on Sunday said the law was on the state's side. Kharge went on to add that that both Karnataka and Tamil Nadu would have to abide by the Supreme Court's directions. His remarks come amid a row over the project, with the BJP accusing the Congress of adopting different positions.

Article Title: IndiGo flight’s landing gear fails to retract after take-off, makes safe emergency landing in Pune
Article Text:
The aircraft conducted a low pass over the runway to facilitate a visual assessment of the landing gear

PUNE: A full emergency was declared at the Pune airport on Sunday morning after a Guwahati bound IndiGo flight (6E 0623) with 192 persons on board, including passengers and crew, reported a technical issue shortly after take-off.The pilot informed Air Traffic Control (ATC) that the aircraft’s landing gear (undercarriage) had failed to retract after take-off and remained in the extended position. Airport officials said that immediately upon receiving the information, they coordinated with ATC, IndiGo and all concerned agencies."The Indian Air Force (IAF) declared a Full Emergency, following which all prescribed emergency response procedures were promptly activated. Fire services, ambulance services and other emergency response teams were placed on high alert to ensure the safety of passengers and crew," Pune airport director Santosh Dhoke said.As a precautionary measure, the aircraft conducted a low pass over the runway to facilitate a visual assessment of the landing gear. Subsequently, the aircraft landed safely at Pune Airport at around 9am."Following the landing, the aircraft was escorted to Bay number- 7 by three fire-fighting vehicles and two ambulances, in accordance with the prescribed emergency response procedures.After confirmation of the aircraft’s safe and normal status, ATC declared the full emergency withdrawn at 9.10am. Thereafter, the aerobridge was connected, and all passengers were safely deboarded," the director added.All 192 persons on board, including passengers and crew, were safe, and no injuries were reported. IndiGo is arranging an alternate aircraft from Bengaluru to Pune to facilitate the onward journey of the affected passengers to Guwahati.
Article Summary: A full emergency was declared at the Pune airport on Sunday morning after a Guwahati bound IndiGo flight reported a technical issue. The pilot informed Air Traffic Control that the aircraft’s landing gear (undercarriage) had failed to retract after take-off. The aircraft conducted a low pass over the runway to facilitate a visual assessment of the landing gear. Subsequently, the aircraft landed safely at Pune Airport at around 9am.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A spate of disturbing ragging complaints by first-year MBBS students - ranging from being forced to imitate sexual acts, change clothes in front of others to late-night humiliation and social boycotts - has prompted National Medical Commission (NMC) to issue 18 notices or communications to 15 medical colleges between Oct 16 and Nov 11.The complaints, received by NMC's anti-ragging cell, concern 14 colleges in Rajasthan and one in Karnataka. They allege physical and verbal abuse, sexual humiliation, coercive activities, restrictions on juniors' movement, and threats of academic retaliation.The action comes amid a separate ragging case at Govt Medical College, Jalaun, UP, where videos of alleged harassment of junior students surfaced online in Oct.The college initially suspended seven senior students for a week. Following a wider inquiry, 10 more were found involved, taking the total to 17 students, who were subsequently suspended for three months and fined Rs 25,000 each.In most cases, NMC sought detailed action taken reports within 24 hours, directing colleges to identify those involved, preserve footage from CCTV cameras and digital evidence, conduct impartial inquiries and protect complainants from intimidation.It has advised colleges to take the strictest action against students found guilty, including suspension or cancellation of their medical registration, an NMC official told TOI. Citing Gujarat as an example, he said some students' registrations had been suspended there.He stressed that enforcement largely rested with state authorities and medical councils, adding lenient approach has often allowed offenders to escape action. "NMC will support the harshest action, provided due process is followed," the official said.Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson United Doctors Front said, "Young students enter medical colleges to build their future, not to face intimidation and exploitation. State govts must act immediately, order independent probes and hold college authorities accountable. No institution can be allowed to shield abuse in the name of tradition."Some complaints describe particularly disturbing incidents. In Rajasthan's Banswara Govt Medical College, first-year students were allegedly forced to perform degrading postures, imitate sexual acts, dance to 'item' songs and change clothes in front of others. At Churu, complaints included forced haircuts, removal of clothing and sexual humiliation.Other complaints cited coercive instructions in a "Personality Development Program" document at Sardar Patel Medical College, Bikaner, and alleged emotional and verbal abuse, with possible faculty involvement, at Karnataka's Ballari Medical College.NMC has directed the colleges to conduct confidential student interviews, provide counselling and prevent retaliation against complainants. It has also sought details of the functioning of their anti-ragging committees and squads.
Article Summary: National Medical Commission issues 18 notices or communications to 15 medical colleges. Complaints received concern 14 colleges in Rajasthan and one in Karnataka. They allege physical and verbal abuse, sexual humiliation, coercive activities, restrictions on juniors' movement, and threats of academic retaliation.

Article Title: 'Completely false': NCP (SP) rejects merger buzz after Supriya Sule says talks ended with Ajit Pawar's death
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Sharad Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party (NCP-SP) on Saturday dismissed reports of a possible merger with the Ajit Pawar-led faction as "completely false", saying it had no plans to merge with any other political party.NCP (SP) spokesperson Pravin Kunte Patil alleged that the reports were being deliberately circulated to divert public attention from pressing issues such as drought, inflation, unemployment, alleged vote theft and irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) examinations."Our official stand is that those who wish to merge should join our party," Kunte Patil said, PTI reported.His remarks came amid renewed speculation about a possible reunion between the two NCP factions: the one led by Sharad Pawar and the other headed by Maharashtra Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar.Earlier in the day, NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule said discussions about a merger had ended for her following the death of her cousin, former NCP chief Ajit Pawar . She also said she had received no communication from leaders of the other faction on the matter.Speaking to reporters, Sule said merger discussions had taken place when Ajit Pawar was alive and that a date had even been decided. However, she said the discussions came to an end after his death."When my brother (then NCP chief Ajit Pawar) was alive, there were discussions about a merger. A date had also been decided. But the day my brother passed away, the merger issue came to a full stop for me and within our party," Sule said.She said her party had neither made any announcement on a merger after Ajit Pawar's death nor responded to statements from the other faction."No spokesperson from our side has spoken on this issue in the last several months," she said. Sule also said she had received no communication from the Ajit Pawar faction about a possible merger."Not a single phone call, WhatsApp message, SMS, letter or email has come to me from anyone in the Ajit Pawar faction regarding a merger. Nobody has contacted me. No one has met me regarding this," she added.Sule said her relationship with Ajit Pawar was based on affection and not political considerations, adding that she did not see the point of discussing a merger after his death."For you, this may be a discussion or gossip. For us, these are emotions. Some things are done from the heart. My relationship with my brother was that of love and affection. He is no longer here. What is the point of discussing it now?" she said.Asked whether talks could be held with Ajit Pawar's family, including his wife Sunetra Pawar, Sule said personal relationships should not be mixed with politics.Sule also rejected speculation that the NCP (SP) could join the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA)."There has been no discussion on joining the NDA. When there has been no beginning, where does the question of a full stop arise?" she said.She declined to comment on statements made by senior leaders of the Ajit Pawar faction, including Chhagan Bhujbal, Sunil Tatkare, Praful Patel and Hasan Mushrif."These are senior leaders who have worked with my father. I am much younger than them in age and experience. The values my parents taught me are that one should not speak disrespectfully about people who are older or more experienced," she said.Expressing frustration over repeated questions about a possible merger, Sule urged the media to focus on policy issues and hold political leaders accountable. She said she was "already bored with the subject"."There are several important issues facing the country and the world. There are serious policy-making issues that need to be discussed. The FCRA Bill, One Nation, One Election and several other important issues are before us.We should be discussing these issues," she said.On her meetings with senior NCP leader Praful Patel, Sule said they were related to parliamentary committee work and had no political significance."I am a member of the Finance Committee and he is also involved in committee work. We also meet in connection with the JPC on the FCRA. These are institutional meetings, not political discussions," she added.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) spokesperson Pravin Kunte Patil alleged that the reports were being deliberately circulated to divert public attention from pressing issues. Sule said merger discussions had taken place when Ajit Pawar was alive and that a date had even been decided. She said the discussions came to an end after his death.

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) spokesperson Manoj Pandey on Sunday backed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi 's criticism of the BJP-led government, alleging that India was witnessing an undeclared Emergency, with democratic values, citizens' rights and press freedom coming under threat.Reacting to Gandhi's remarks at the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad, Pandey said concerns over the state of democracy in India were being raised at several national and international platforms."This issue is being raised on several national and international platforms and is also being discussed abroad. Constitutional institutions are being manipulated to remain in power," he said.The remarks come amid a political row over Gandhi's comments at the summit on Saturday, where he alleged that democracy in India was "destroyed" in 2014 and questioned the credibility of the electoral process.Addressing the gathering, the Congress leader claimed that the flow of large amounts of money into the political system had fundamentally changed the electoral landscape in 2014. Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission (EC) has told the Supreme Court that it remains committed to ensuring that all eligible voters find their names in electoral rolls while simultaneously addressing inconsistencies in the lists during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise."There have been and will be problems that arise from time to time and the Commission remains alive to the need to ensure that those who are eligible to vote find their names in the voters' lists but equally, at the same time, to ensure that all inconsistencies in these lists are addressed," the poll panel said in an affidavit filed before the Supreme Court, as reported by news agency PTI.The EC said voters whose names were missing from the draft electoral rolls despite being enrolled in previous electoral rolls could apply afresh using Form 6 without facing prosecution, provided they were not already registered in another parliamentary or assembly constituency and their declarations complied with the law.The clarification came after concerns were raised that such applicants could face prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, for submitting Form 6 despite having been registered earlier. The Commission said it had asked chief electoral officers to publicise the clarification widely, including in local languages.According to PTI, the EC also informed the court that it had taken note of its suggestion to reach out to voters categorised as ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate) to facilitate their inclusion in electoral rolls.In a communication dated November 6, 2026, the Commission directed chief electoral officers in states and Union territories where the SIR is underway to allow voters to submit duly filled Enumeration Forms to the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) or Booth Level Officer (BLO) at their current ordinary residence.Voters who have not shifted can submit a signed Enumeration Form along with a statement explaining why they had not submitted it earlier. The documents can be submitted personally or through family members. An online submission facility with e-sign is also available on ECINET.The EC said it had directed the creation of a mechanism to ensure that no eligible elector was deprived of an opportunity to have their name included in the final electoral roll, while also preventing duplicate registrations.The Commission said the exercise involved challenges because of the large number of voters and the digitalisation of electoral data. It maintained that ensuring the purity of the electoral process and protecting the voting rights of eligible citizens remained its constitutional responsibility.
Article Summary: The Election Commission (EC) has told the Supreme Court that it remains committed to ensuring that all eligible voters find their names in electoral rolls. It said voters whose names were missing from the draft electoral rolls despite being enrolled in previous electoral rolls could apply afresh using Form 6.

NEW DELHI: Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh on Saturday chaired a high-level security review meeting after fresh violence in the state claimed five lives, including four civilians in Ukhrul district.This came after on Friday, a woman was killed in Taphou Kuki village in Kangpokpi district, while four people were shot dead at New Heaven in Ukhrul.The meeting reviewed the law and order situation and discussed measures to strengthen security, particularly in vulnerable areas.It was decided that combing operations would continue to apprehend those involved in criminal activities, a statement said, PTI reported.Security forces were also directed to strengthen security in their respective areas of deployment. The meeting was attended by home minister Govindas Konthoujam, chief secretary Rajeev Singh Thakur, DGP Mukesh Singh, senior officers of the Assam Rifles, CRPF and BSF, and representatives of other central agencies.Meanwhile, Naga People's Front (NPF) MLA Leishiyo Keishing demanded strict action against those responsible for the killing of four civilians in Ukhrul.Keishing made the demand during a visit to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS) in Imphal, where the bodies of the victims were brought for post-mortem examination.He appealed to civil society organisations, village authorities and youth leaders to initiate dialogue and work towards restoring peace. He cautioned that retaliatory violence would only lead to further loss of innocent lives.Family members of the deceased gathered at the JNIMS mortuary complex to pay floral tributes. A large number of people also took to the streets to pay their respects to the four victims, who belonged to the Tangkhul Naga community.The Tangkhul Naga Long (TNL), the community's apex body, issued a three-day ultimatum to the state government, demanding that "Kuki militants" be driven out of Naga-inhabited areas.The organisation also called for the immediate withdrawal of all central security forces deployed in the area and the transfer of the case to the National Investigation Agency (NIA).It warned that if its demands were not met within three days, it would launch an indefinite public agitation until justice was delivered.
Article Summary: The meeting reviewed the law and order situation and discussed measures to strengthen security. It was decided that combing operations would continue to apprehend those involved in criminal activities. Naga People's Front (NPF) MLA Leishiyo Keishing demanded strict action against those responsible for the killing of four civilians in Ukhrul.

Article Title: PMO steps in after fake court orders lead to blocking of 129 betting websites

NEW DELHI: PM Modi 's office on Saturday summoned telecommunications secretary Amit Agrawal, seeking an explanation over how more than 100 websites were blocked on the basis of fake court orders, two government officials told news agency Reuters.On Wednesday, telecom officials had directed internet providers to block 129 illegal betting websites using fabricated high court orders, as per the report. The documents had been emailed to officials by individuals posing as lawyers.PM Modi's office has sought an explanation from Agrawal over the lapse, with the summons also cutting short the telecom secretary's visit to another state, the two officials familiar with the matter said.The development marks increased scrutiny of the episode, which has raised questions about the safeguards in India's website-blocking system. While online betting is illegal in the country, the use of forged court documents to initiate takedown orders has raised concerns that legitimate websites could also be targeted.Agrawal is the senior-most bureaucrat in the telecommunications ministry, which oversees major telecom operators and internet service providers."The action taken by the Department of Telecommunications against betting accounts was carried out through the relevant field officers," one of the officials said.The controversy has also led to a criminal investigation by state police into suspected forgery and cheating by unidentified individuals. On Friday, Reuters reported that the telecommunications ministry had started an internal investigation into the alleged fraud. Police have also sought records from the ministry as part of their probe.The two state court orders identified as fake by Reuters, based on comments from police and the court registry, carried fabricated court logos and seals, along with a fake QR code.Both documents had remained available on the Department of Telecommunications' website for months. They were published alongside correspondence showing officials directing internet providers to take down the websites.As of Saturday, one of the fake orders was still accessible on the government website, while the other had been removed.The episode comes amid wider concerns among judges across the world over fabricated legal precedents, including those generated using artificial intelligence.In July, India's Supreme Court set aside a tribunal's orders that relied on non-existent judgments. A US judge recently disqualified lawyers over the use of fabricated legal citations.Last year, India's Supreme Court justices also warned against the fabrication of judicial documents, saying such acts "bearing forged signatures of Judges strikes at the very foundation of public trust" and "such grave criminal acts cannot be treated as ordinary or routine offences".

On Wednesday, telecom officials had directed internet providers to block 129 illegal betting websites. The documents had been emailed to officials by individuals posing as lawyers.

Article Title: From kidneys to body tissues: Desperate Iranians put organs up for sale as war drags on, claims report

Iran's worsening economic crisis is pushing some residents to desperate lengths, with people offering to sell multiple organs and body tissues, including kidneys, bone marrow, testicles and corneas, to escape mounting debts and meet basic household expenses. An investigation by Iran International has found a growing online market in which financially distressed Iranians are advertising body parts for sale, with some even willing to part with vital organs to secure their families' futures.The findings come as Iran faces mounting economic pressure amid the lingering conflict in the Middle East, a US naval blockade and stringent sanctions. With little clarity over when the standoff between Tehran and Washington will ease, concerns are growing over the impact of prolonged economic uncertainty on ordinary Iranians. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has reportedly warned that the pressure could continue indefinitely, while predicting further deterioration in Iran's economy over the coming months, according to Al Jazeera.Iran International examined more than 600 advertisements posted on a Telegram channel between late May and late October. Its investigation found that approximately one in three advertisements offered more than one organ or type of body tissue.Kidneys were the most frequently advertised, featuring in 498 listings. Bone marrow appeared in 279 advertisements, followed by liver in 51, testicles in 15 and corneas in two. In 142 listings, sellers offered both kidneys and bone marrow, while another 26 advertised kidneys, bone marrow and liver together.Some advertisements also raised questions about whether sellers understood the medical procedures they were proposing. One man offering several body parts, including a testicle, told Iran International: "I can still live after losing these organs." He appeared unaware that some of the procedures he was offering were not established transplant options in Iran.Interviews with prospective sellers revealed the financial desperation behind the listings. One man said he was willing to give up even vital organs to secure his young daughter's future. Another, a former clothing business owner, said bankruptcy had left him with mounting debts and bounced cheques. He hoped selling an organ would help him repay at least some of his liabilities.Others described struggling with years of renting accommodation or simply trying to afford everyday necessities. A single mother raising two daughters said she was searching for a buyer to support her family's basic expenses.The situation is unfolding as Washington reportedly shifts towards sustained economic pressure on Tehran after months of fighting and negotiations.According to Al Jazeera, Rubio told G7 counterparts in Paris that a naval blockade, stringent sanctions and disruptions to overland trade could remain in place without a clear end date.Tehran-based economist Isaac Saidian warned that if the economic siege pushes Iran's oil revenues close to zero, the government could face one of the most difficult periods in its recent history. The challenge, he said, would extend beyond foreign currency shortages to paying salaries and pensions, supplying essential goods and preventing further inflation.President Masoud Pezeshkian's administration has prepared for the possibility of prolonged restrictions, although Iranian authorities have rejected suggestions of an impending economic collapse.Meanwhile, military tensions remain a concern. The IRGC has claimed responsibility for drone attacks targeting a US air defence radar installation in Bahrain, while Iranian forces have also reported oil tankers catching fire after striking naval mines around the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: Investigation finds growing online market in which financially distressed Iranians are advertising body parts for sale. One in three advertisements offered more than one organ or type of body tissue. Kidneys were the most frequently advertised, featuring in 498 listings. Bone marrow appeared in 279 advertisements, followed by liver in 51, testicles in 15 and corneas in two.

CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu government has suspended five library officials over the procurement of AI-generated books for the Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore.According to an announcement made by school education minister A Rajmohan on Sunday, those suspended are S Kamatchi, chief librarian, Anna Centenary Library (ACL), Chennai; Dinesh Kumar, chief librarian and information officer (in-charge), Kalaignar Centenary Library, Madurai; V Santhanakrishnan, librarian and information officer, Kalaignar Centenary Library, Madurai, and in-charge of the Periyar Arivulagam Library; S Santhana Karthikeyan, librarian and information officer, ACL, Chennai; and J Juliet, chief accounts officer, Directorate of Public Libraries.The minister said the irregularities had occurred during the previous DMK regime.The alleged irregularities came to light after writer Perumal Murugan identified nearly 1,800 books from Agal Vilakku Pathippagam in the library’s fourth-floor Tamil section.The books reportedly carried inflated prices, AI-generated misinformation, fictitious author names and invalid International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs).Writers and researchers subsequently flagged similar irregularities elsewhere.Researchers have also raised concerns about the library’s English-language books. BALLIA: A 28-year-old police sub-inspector died by suicide on a railway track here, allegedly after being blackmailed by a woman, an officer said on Sunday.The sub-inspector, identified as Sandeep Kumar, was posted at the Chitbarhagaon police station in Ballia, news agency PTI reported.SP Iraj Raja said police received information on Saturday night, between 7pm and 8pm, that a person had died by suicide by lying on a railway track.The information was mentioned in an MRO report filed by a railway loco pilot at the next station. Article Title: UP horror: 3 siblings returning from Haryana killed as pickup hits bike, brick-laden tractor runs them over amid dense fog

An 18-year-old boy and his two elder sisters tragically died in a collision in Sitapur district

LUCKNOW: An 18-year-old teenager and his two sisters, aged 18 and 19, were killed after their motorcycle was hit by a speeding pickup vehicle and subsequently run over by an overloaded, brick-laden tractor-trailer amid poor visibility in Sitapur district early Sunday morning.The accident occurred around 6am near a petrol pump in the Rihar area under the Tambaur police station limits.Dense fog and low visibility reportedly reduced visibility on the road, leaving little room for the victims to escape the impact of the collision. All three died on the spot.The deceased were identified as Shishupal, 18, son of Tuka Ram, and his sisters Pooja Devi, 19, and Gayatri Devi, 18. All three belonged to Devpalpur village in the Tambaur area of Sitapur.According to information, the siblings had gone to Haryana to work as labourers and returned to Laharpur late Saturday night.Two residents of their village had reportedly reached Laharpur on separate motorcycles to receive them. On Sunday morning, Shishupal took both his sisters on his motorcycle and set off for their native village.However, when they reached near a petrol pump in Rihar, a speeding pickup allegedly rammed into their motorcycle amid the poor visibility.The impact threw all three onto the road. Before they could move to safety, an overloaded tractor-trailer carrying bricks ran over them, leaving them with fatal injuries.According to local residents, none of the three siblings was wearing a helmet at the time of the accident.The incident triggered panic in the area, with residents gathering at the spot after seeing the bodies lying on the road. The police were alerted and reached the scene shortly afterwards.The police took custody of the bodies and sent them for post-mortem examinations to complete the necessary legal formalities.Tambaur station house officer Pradeep Singh said the police were searching for the tractor-trailer and its driver.Further action would be taken after tracing the vehicle and establishing the circumstances leading to the accident.
Article Summary: An 18-year-old boy and his two elder sisters tragically died in a collision in Sitapur district early Sunday morning. Dense fog and low visibility reportedly reduced visibility on the road, leaving little room for the victims to escape the impact of the collision. All three died on the spot.

Article Title: Relationship since 2016, marriage fixed elsewhere: UP man storms woman's home, stabs her, mother and grandmother

LUCKNOW: A 26-year-old man allegedly stormed into a woman’s house and stabbed her, her mother and grandmother following a dispute over her impending marriage to another man in Bahraich late Saturday night.The accused, identified as Arzaan Qureshi, 23, was arrested by the police, Superintendent of Police Vishwajeet Srivastava told TOI.All three women sustained serious stab injuries and were rushed to the district hospital. The condition of the woman, who had earlier lodged a molestation and harassment complaint against the accused, was stated to be critical.According to the SP, Arzaan and the woman had been in a relationship since 2016. He was reportedly angry after learning that her marriage had been fixed with someone else, which allegedly triggered the attack.The incident took place around 11pm in the Dargah police station area of Bahraich city.According to preliminary information, the woman had lodged an FIR against Arzaan around six years ago on charges of molestation and harassment.A case had also been registered against him under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.He was arrested in connection with the case and subsequently released on bail, after which he reportedly left the area.Police said Arzaan arrived at the woman’s house late Saturday night and knocked on the door while disguising his voice. When the woman’s younger sister opened the door, he allegedly pushed her aside and forcibly entered the house.He then attacked the woman with a knife. When her mother and grandmother rushed to intervene and rescue her, the accused allegedly attacked them as well, leaving all three seriously injured.Hearing their screams, neighbours rushed to the house, but the accused had already fled. Local residents subsequently arranged for the injured women to be taken to the district hospital for treatment.Following information about the incident, city circle officer Narayan Dutt Mishra and Dargah station house officer Amitendra Singh reached the hospital and took stock of the situation.Confirming the earlier case against Arzaan, CO City Narayan Dutt Mishra said a molestation case, along with provisions of the POCSO Act, had been registered against him six years ago.The SP subsequently confirmed to TOI that Arzaan had been arrested. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the attack and the relationship between the accused and the woman.
Article Summary: A 26-year-old man allegedly stormed into a woman's house and stabbed her, her mother and grandmother following a dispute over her impending marriage. The accused, identified as Arzaan Qureshi, 23, was arrested by the police. The woman, who had earlier lodged a molestation and harassment complaint against the accused, was stated to be critical.

Article Title: 'Bomb planted at CSMT': Security agencies, dog squad launch hours-long search after caller warns of blast at Mumbai station

A bomb threat was reported at CSMT on Saturday evening; security agencies conducted a thorough search of the station premises after the alert

MUMBAI: A major security operation was launched at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) on Saturday evening after authorities received a phone call warning of a bomb blast at the busy railway station. The threat, however, turned out to be a hoax after an extensive search of the premises.According to officials, the Government Railway Police (GRP) Control Room at Wadi Bunder received information around 6.40pm about a caller claiming that an explosive device had been planted at CSMT.Following the alert, multiple security agencies swung into action and initiated a comprehensive combing operation across the station.Teams from the Railway Protection Force (RPF), Government Railway Police, Mumbai Police and other security units carried out a coordinated search of the station complex.An RPF dog squad was also deployed to scan key areas, including suburban and long-distance train platforms, foot overbridges and the parcel office.Security personnel thoroughly checked parked trains and various sections of the station to ensure passenger safety.The operation continued for several hours amid heightened vigilance, though railway services were not disrupted.Central Railway chief spokesperson Swapnil Nila said that no suspicious object, explosive material or suspect individual was found during the search.Following the exhaustive sweep, officials declared the bomb threat a hoax.Authorities are now working to trace the caller and determine the source of the threatening message.They reiterated that strict action would be taken against those responsible for creating panic and misusing emergency response systems.
Article Summary: A bomb threat was reported at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) on Saturday evening. Authorities received a phone call warning of a bomb blast at the busy railway station. The threat, however, turned out to be a hoax after an extensive search of the premises.

Article Title: Pakistani handler used romantic relationship to recruit woman for Rajasthan Railway track blast: Probe
Article Text:
Accused Davinder Singh (23), and 21-year-old woman Mahakdeep Kaur

JAISALMER: The conspiracy behind the November 3 blast on a railway track near 50 GB village in Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district was allegedly masterminded by a Pakistan-based ISI handler identified as Shah, who used a romantic relationship to recruit a young woman to carry out the attack.The accused were allegedly paid Rs 2.23 lakh for executing the operation, including Rs 1 lakh in cash, while the remaining amount was transferred to their bank accounts.The primary objective behind the railway track blast, allegedly orchestrated by the ISI, was to spread terror across Rajasthan, particularly in Sri Ganganagar.ADGP ATS Dinesh MN, along with senior officials of AGTF, ANTF, Bikaner Range IG Om Prakash and Sri Ganganagar SP Harishankar, disclosed details of the investigation at a press conference on Sunday.The Rajasthan Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Sri Ganganagar police, with assistance from Punjab Counter Intelligence, arrested two accused, including 21-year-old Mahakdeep Kaur and Davinder Singh (23), from Gurdaspur in Punjab.Police recovered two foreign-made pistols, 46 live cartridges and Rs 30,000 in cash from the arrested accused.Dinesh MN said the blast was carried out at the direction of a foreign-based handler whose objective was to spread panic in Sri Ganganagar and across Rajasthan.The handler allegedly provided the target location, funding and instructions for executing the attack.Investigations revealed that Mahakdeep Kaur had married around two years ago, but her marriage ended in December 2024. In February 2025, her husband, Karanveer Singh, was jailed in an NDPS case. Subsequently, he re-established contact with her and allegedly asked her to communicate with a Pakistan-based person named Lovely, who would provide money to be delivered to him in jail.Lovely later introduced her to another person identified as Shah. Gradually, conversations between Mahakdeep and Shah developed into a romantic relationship, and she became emotionally attached to him. The Pakistani handler allegedly exploited this relationship to recruit her for the railway blast and assign her targets.According to the ADGP, Mahakdeep and Davinder visited the Ramsinghpur area on October 6, but their first attempt failed because explosives were not available. They returned on October 12 or 13 with explosives and a timer, but a technical malfunction prevented the blast. Following further instructions from Pakistan, they allegedly succeeded in triggering the explosion near 50 GB on November 3. Investigators are also examining whether a train was the intended target.The breakthrough came after an extensive investigation involving the analysis of nearly five lakh call records and the questioning of more than 400 people. Police also examined suspected Pakistan-linked smugglers and their local contacts before tracing the accused through technical surveillance and human intelligence.Dinesh MN said inputs from central agencies received three days ago led ATS teams to Punjab. With assistance from Punjab Counter Intelligence, the suspects' locations were traced to Gurdaspur, where they were arrested on November 15.Both accused will be produced before a court and taken on remand for further interrogation to identify other members of the network and establish links with Pakistan-based handlers.
Article Summary: The primary objective behind the railway track blast, allegedly orchestrated by the ISI, was to spread terror across Rajasthan, particularly in Sri Ganganagar. Police recovered two foreign-made pistols, 46 live cartridges and Rs 30,000 in cash from the arrested accused. Both accused will be produced before a court and taken on remand for further interrogation.

Article Title: Woman buys Rs 1,755 pressure cooker, finds rice and dal remain uncooked despite 3-4 whistles; consumer commission orders refund, Rs 12,000 compensation and Rs 3,000 costs, imposes Rs 21,000 penalty on

HYDERABAD: A pressure cooker bought for Rs 1,755 was supposed to make everyday cooking easier. Instead, a woman in Visakhapatnam found that rice remained partially uncooked even after three to four whistles. When the same problem persisted while preparing dal the following day, she approached the seller for help. The dispute eventually landed before a consumer commission, which ordered the store, dealer and manufacturer to pay her Rs 16,755.The Visakhapatnam District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ruled that the woman was entitled to a refund of the product's cost, along with compensation and litigation expenses, after finding deficiencies in the services provided by the three parties.The commission, presided over by Gudla Tanuja, with members Varri Krishna Murthy and Rahimunnisa Begum, passed the order on October 31. The woman had purchased a four-litre deep-pan pressure cooker from a store for Rs 1,755, paying through UPI. She said she first noticed the problem when she used it to cook rice on the day of purchase. Despite allowing the cooker to function for the prescribed three to four whistles, the rice was only partially cooked.An attempt to prepare dal the next day yielded the same result, according to her complaint. She then contacted the store, alleging that its staff responded insensitively and asked her to approach the company's service centre. However, citing her age and physical limitations, she said she could not visit the centre. The store subsequently collected the cooker from her and issued a service bill for its repair. But the woman maintained that she wanted a replacement rather than a repair. The company later informed her that it had instructed the dealer to replace the appliance, but the dealer had not acted on the instruction, the commission noted.The store and the dealer maintained that the cooker had been examined by service personnel, who had even shared a video demonstrating that it was working properly. Their lawyers told the commission that the woman had refused an offer to accompany her to the service centre for a demonstration. They also argued that she had insisted on a replacement despite the appliance being in working condition and was seeking an excessive amount as compensation.The store and dealer further contended that she had not submitted an expert opinion or technical report to establish a manufacturing defect. They also accused her of threatening litigation and claiming to have connections with consumer commission personnel. The manufacturer, meanwhile, argued that its warranty obligations were limited to repairing or replacing products with inherent manufacturing defects. It maintained that the cooker had undergone operational testing and was found to be functioning properly.The commission observed that the store, dealer and manufacturer had failed to produce the warranty terms before it. It also questioned their reliance on a proposed replacement as a goodwill gesture, asking why such an offer would have been made if the appliance had no problem. The bench held that the woman was entitled to a refund as a consumer exercising her legal rights under the Consumer Protection Act, and not merely because the company was willing to offer a goodwill replacement.It also took exception to the allegations that she had used purported connections within the commission to threaten the store and dealer. Describing the remarks as defamatory, the commission said they amounted to an attempt to tarnish the institution's image and included derogatory comments about the complainant.The commission directed the store, dealer and manufacturer to refund the Rs 1,755 paid for the cooker, pay Rs 12,000 as compensation for deficiency in service and bear Rs 3,000 towards litigation costs. Separately, the store and dealer were directed to pay a penalty of Rs 21,000 to the Andhra Pradesh State Legal Services Authority in Amaravati for making what the commission described as baseless allegations about its functioning.
Article Summary: A woman in Visakhapatnam found that rice remained partially uncooked even after three to four whistles. The dispute eventually landed before a consumer commission, which ordered the store, dealer and manufacturer to pay her Rs 16,755. The commission ruled that the woman was entitled to a refund of the product's cost.

Article Title: How scrap dealer lured ex-Tech Mahindra regional head Paramjeet Dhankar to his death: 'Brother, brother, please’, 14 bullets, magazine change'
Article Text:
CCTV footage shows the sequence of events that led to the cold-blooded murder on Nov 7.

How past disputes culminated in Faridabad shooting

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





FARIDABAD: “Dhankar sahab, please come out for a moment. I need to park my car,” scrap dealer Mohan Sharma urged his neighbour Paramjeet Dhankar, a senior vice-president with Singapore-based FPT Software who had returned to his Faridabad home just a day earlier to attend his nephew’s wedding.Minutes later, as the two walked outside the main gate, Sharma pumped nine bullets into Dhankar, reports. As the senior IT executive staggered towards the road, trying to escape, Sharma pursued him, continued firing and even changed his magazine as bullets ran out. He then shouted, “Happy Diwali. I will kill everyone today.”Sharma did not stop even after Dhankar slumped to the ground. He fired at his son, who escaped behind parked cars. The incident took place just 500m from the police commissioner’s office.CCTV footage shows the sequence of events that led to the cold-blooded murder on Nov 7. According to police, Sharma, a scrap dealer, fired 14 rounds from his licensed pistol. Dhankar, an ex-Asia Pacific head of Tech Mahindra, died before he could be wheeled into hospital.The killing followed weeks of friction between the two families, who lived in the same building in Sector 21C and shared its parking area.Dhankar’s family occupied the ground floor, Sharma lived on the second, and two other families occupied the first and top floors. With four households competing for space, parking had repeatedly triggered arguments, a relative told TOI.According to police, there was also tension between the two families over Sharma’s pet dog. Dhankar’s son had objected to the dog defecating in the common parking area.An earlier confrontation on Oct 22 had further soured relations. Sharma allegedly damaged the gate of Dhankar’s house, an incident captured on the family’s CCTV cameras. The family gave the footage to police, who called Sharma to the station and allegedly reprimanded him.But another confrontation took place at the local police station on the day of the murder. Sources said Dhankar’s friends and aides confronted Sharma, abused and manhandled him. Both sides returned home at 6pm. But the humiliation is likely to have fuelled his anger.Later that evening, Sharma rang the bell at Dhankar’s house and repeatedly urged him to come downstairs and move his car. Dhankar came down with his son, Shaurya. In the footage, Sharma is heard addressing him as “Dhankar sahab” and repeatedly saying, “Brother, brother, brother, please.”The exchange turned hostile. When Dhankar suggested he did not want to continue the conversation, Shaurya began moving towards the staircase. Sharma allegedly stopped him and asked him to return. He then pulled out his licensed .45 ACP pistol, fitted with an extended magazine, and fired.Dhankar tried to get away, staggering from the garage towards the road. Sharma dashed towards him, firing as he went. As Dhankar fell outside the building, his wife rushed out. But Sharma continued firing and changed the magazine. He then threatened the family and called out to them to come outside.Dhankar returned from Singapore on Nov 5 for his nephew’s wedding in Meerut.Police arrested Sharma near DLF Chowk in Ballabhgarh the next day and seized the weapon. A case was registered against him under BNS sections 103 (murder), 109 (attempt to murder) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy).
Article Summary: Mohan Sharma, a scrap dealer, fired 14 rounds from his licensed pistol. Paramjeet Dhankar, an ex-Asia Pacific head of Tech Mahindra, died before he could be wheeled into hospital. The killing followed weeks of friction between the two families who lived in the same building in Sector 21C.

Article Title: Curtains drawn on NCP(SP)-NCP merger after Ajit Pawar's death, received no fresh proposal: Supriya Sule
Article Text:
Supriya Sule, the working president of NCP (SP), has ruled out any potential merger between the party factions

PUNE: NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule on Thursday ruled out any merger between the Sharad Pawar-led NCP and the rival party led by the late Ajit Pawar , saying she had decided to “draw the curtains” on the issue following her cousin’s death and had received no fresh merger proposal.Supriya’s remarks come amid renewed efforts by several NCP seniors to revive merger discussions and speculation over possible rapprochement between the two parties. On Wednesday, NCP president Sunetra Pawar declined to clarify the possibility of a merger between the two NCPs, saying matters would become clear at the appropriate time.“Discussions on the merger were on when Ajit Pawar was alive, and the entire world knew about them. A video of one such meeting held on Jan 17 was also circulated in the media,” Supriya said.“The day my cousin died, and following the developments that unfolded a few days after his death, I decided to draw the curtains on the issue of merger. I do not think I should speak much on the topic. It ended with my cousin’s death,” she said.After Ajit Pawar’s death in a plane crash on Jan 28, senior leaders of his party had denied holding any meetings with the Sharad Pawar-led party to discuss a merger.However, state NCP president Sunil Tatkare recently said he was aware of the talks and claimed that the merger would have taken place had Ajit Pawar been alive.Tatkare and state minister Hasan Mushrif on Thursday said they would soon meet Sharad Pawarin Mumbai, fuelling further speculation about efforts to bring the two parties together.“I will meet Pawar Saheb to enquire about his health when I visit Mumbai. He is our mentor, and I do not think there is anything wrong with any member of our party meeting him for personal reasons,” Tatkare said.On the merger issue, Mushrif said the decision would be taken by his party chief, Sunetra Pawar. “We will abide by the decision Sunetra Pawar takes on the merger,” he said.Responding to Shiv Sena neta Sanjay Shirsat’s suggestion that a third faction could emerge in NCP, Mushrif said attempts were being made to weaken the party after Ajit Pawar’s death. Mushrif added that he would approach deputy CM Eknath Shinde and urge him to caution members of his party (Shiv Sena) against targeting NCP.
Article Summary: Supriya Sule, the working president of NCP (SP), has ruled out any potential merger between the party factions. Her remarks come amid renewed efforts by several NCP seniors to revive merger discussions and speculation over possible rapprochement between the two parties.

BENGALURU: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Bengaluru on Friday to inaugurate the Namma Metro Pink Line and attend the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram, which also mark the birth centenary of author HV Sheshadri.The programme at S-VYASA University, organised by the S-VYASA Registered Society, is scheduled to begin at 10am. Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.
